name: Pygments
description: The reference Python highlighter; huge lexer catalog, many formatters (HTML, LaTeX, RTF, SVG, image, ANSI), and the ancestor of several ports

form-factor.comment: Usable as a library and via the bundled `pygmentize` / `python -m pygments` command-line tool.

license.comment: License-Expression BSD-2-Clause on PyPI; lexers and styles are part of the same package under the same licence.

documentation.comment: Dedicated docs site at pygments.org with quickstart, lexer/formatter development guides, API reference, language list and style gallery.

latest-version.comment: Released 2026-08-17; checked 2026-11-18. 2.22.0 is listed as unreleased in the changelog.

engine-model.comment: Most lexers are RegexLexer state machines (states of regexes on a stack); some lexers are hand-written Python, but regex lexing dominates.

regex-engine.comment: Lexer rules are compiled with Python's standard `re` module (flags default to re.MULTILINE).

embedded-languages.comment: HtmlLexer delegates <script> content to JavascriptLexer (and <style> to CssLexer) via `using()`; DelegatingLexer combines template languages with a host language (e.g. HTML+PHP).

language-auto-detection.comment: `guess_lexer(text)` scores every lexer's `analyse_text()`; `guess_lexer_for_filename` combines filename and content.

filename-extension-mapping.comment: `get_lexer_for_filename` (glob patterns) and `get_lexer_for_mimetype`; `analyse_text` also checks shebangs in many lexers.

resumable-line-state.comment: The RegexLexer state stack is internal; no documented API to save and resume per-line lexer state. Lexing always runs over the full input text.

incremental-reparsing.comment: No edit-aware reparsing; re-lexes the whole input.

semantic-distinctions.comment: Pure regex state-machine lexers; some lexers distinguish e.g. Name.Function at definition sites via regex context, but there is no syntax tree or locals tracking.

bundled-languages.comment: Pygments 2.21.0 homepage: '602 languages and text formats' (checked 2026-11-18). This is the lexer count: it includes ~53 composite template lexers (e.g. 'HTML+Django') and console/session variants, so distinct languages are somewhat fewer (roughly 530-550).

grammar-format.comment: Lexers are Python classes (mostly declarative RegexLexer token tables, sometimes procedural code).

grammar-ecosystem-compatibility.comment: Consumes only Pygments-format lexers (built-in plus third-party plugin packages); no TextMate, Sublime, tree-sitter or KDE grammar support. It is itself the source ecosystem that Chroma and Rouge port from.

runtime-grammar-loading.comment: `load_lexer_from_file()` / `pygmentize -x` load a custom lexer class from a file (evaluated, trusted files only); plugin packages register lexers via entry points; custom lexer classes can also be instantiated directly.

lazy-grammar-loading.comment: Lexer lookup scans the static LEXERS metadata mapping; lexer modules are imported on demand (`_load_lexers`) and cached.

grammar-accuracy.comment: Judgement call: lexers are hand-maintained (not tracking an upstream grammar) but updated steadily for modern syntax (e.g. Python t-strings and TOML 1.1 in 2.20, Python 3.15 in 2.21); regex lexers have recurring gaps on nested/macro constructs (e.g. Rust quote!/keyword-prefix bugs, since fixed). No spot-check run in this pass.

bundled-themes.comment: Style gallery lists 49 styles for 2.21.0 (checked 2026-11-18); the package also ships a special-purpose 'lilypond' style not shown in the gallery (50 in the style mapping).

theme-format.comment: Styles are Python Style subclasses mapping token types to style strings; CSS is generated from them via `get_style_defs`.

token-classification.comment: Hierarchical token types (e.g. Token.Name.Function) with a standard set in STANDARD_TYPES; lexers may create custom subtypes, which styles fall back through parents for.

css-class-output.comment: HtmlFormatter emits short CSS class names by default; `noclasses=True` switches to inline styles.

multi-theme-output.comment: Via class-based HTML output plus per-style stylesheets generated with `get_style_defs(selector)` / `pygmentize -S`; one render can be themed light/dark by swapping or media-scoping stylesheets. No CSS-variable dual-theme mechanism; the wiring is left to the user.

public-token-api.comment: `pygments.lex(code, lexer)` and `Lexer.get_tokens()` return an iterable of (tokentype, value) pairs.

ir-kinds.comment: Flat (tokentype, value) stream; `get_tokens_unprocessed` adds start index. RawTokenFormatter provides a text serialization (not JSON).

serializable-ir.comment: RawTokenFormatter ('raw'/'tokens') writes one 'tokentype<TAB>repr(value)' line per token, optionally gz/bz2-compressed, and the 'raw' lexer reads it back. Documented, but a Pygments-specific text format rather than JSON.

theme-resolved-tokens.comment: Tokens carry only token types. Resolved styles are available by iterating a Style class ((ttype, {color, bold, italic, ...}) tuples), but no API emits tokens with styles already attached; a custom formatter must do the join.

source-offsets-in-ir.comment: `Lexer.get_tokens_unprocessed(text)` yields (index, tokentype, value) with the start position in the input; the higher-level `get_tokens` drops the index. Note that offsets are pre-filter and before option processing.

custom-formatter-api.comment: Subclass `Formatter` and implement `format(tokensource, outfile)`; can be loaded at runtime via `load_formatter_from_file` or plugin entry points.

line-transforms-decorations.comment: Highlighted lines via `hl_lines` (HtmlFormatter, ImageFormatter) and a documented token-stream filter mechanism (e.g. NameHighlightFilter, codetagify, gobble). No built-in diff/focus markers or inline annotations.

output-formats.comment: Built-in formatters: HTML, Terminal (16), Terminal256, TerminalTrueColor, LaTeX, RTF, SVG (experimental), Image (PNG/GIF/JPEG/BMP via Pillow), BBCode, Pango markup, IRC; also Groff/troff, raw tokens, null/text and testcase formatters (no tag).

line-numbers.comment: `linenos` on HTML (table/inline), LaTeX, Terminal, Terminal256, IRC, SVG, RTF, Groff; `line_numbers` on ImageFormatter.

streaming-output.comment: Lexers and formatters are generator/file-based, but `get_tokens` requires the complete input text; there is no documented API to feed input incrementally.

terminal-ready.comment: TerminalFormatter, Terminal256Formatter and TerminalTrueColorFormatter; `pygmentize` CLI uses them directly.

native-dependencies.comment: Pure-Python, py3-none-any wheel with no required dependencies. Optional extras: Pillow for ImageFormatter, colorama for the windows-terminal extra.

runs-in-browser.comment: No first-party browser build; can only run client-side through a third-party Python-in-WASM runtime such as Pyodide.

wasm-build.comment: No official WASM distribution (pure-Python wheel only).

synchronous-api.comment: `highlight()`, `lex()` and `format()` are plain synchronous calls; no async initialisation.

bindings-ports.comment: Ruby: pygments.rb (wrapper talking to a Python child process, under the pygments org). Go: Chroma, a port with translators for Pygments lexers and styles. Rouge (Ruby) is a Pygments-compatible reimplementation and a separate candidate.

core-package-size.comment: Compressed size of pygments-2.21.0-py3-none-any.whl (~1.25 MB). Installed on disk the package is ~5 MB (unpacked from the wheel). All lexers are always included; there is no slim core distribution.

throughput-tier.comment: No independent or reproducible cross-engine benchmark including Pygments was found in this pass.

initialization-cost.comment: No cited measurement of time-to-first-highlight. Lexer modules load lazily, which keeps startup modest, but this is unmeasured.

github-stars.comment: ~2.2k as displayed on GitHub, checked 2026-11-18 (rounded figure). The repository moved to GitHub from Bitbucket in 2019, so stars understate its use.

monthly-downloads.comment: PyPI via pypistats, last month, checked 2026-11-18. Inflated by being a transitive dependency of pip tooling, IPython, rich, pytest, Sphinx and others.

maintenance-status.comment: Releases 2.20.0 (2026-03-29) and 2.21.0 (2026-08-17) with new lexers and fixes; commits through 2026-09-27; PRs merged regularly. Checked 2026-11-18.

documentation-quality.comment: Dedicated docs site with quickstart, lexer/formatter/filter development guides, API reference, language list, style gallery and detailed changelog. No migration guides, and some API (e.g. Style.style_for_token) is underdocumented.

notable-users.value: Sphinx (all code highlighting), MediaWiki SyntaxHighlight extension (Wikimedia projects), Python-Markdown CodeHilite extension

bus-factor.comment: Maintained by Georg Brandl, Matthäus Chajdas and Jean Abou-Samra; recent release and merge activity is mostly by Matthäus Chajdas (Anteru).
